result.description: B2B customer support platform (Slack/email/chat threads, customers, tiers, workflows) with a GraphQL API that matches its UI.
result.auth_detail: Machine-user API keys sent as `Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx`, with fine-grained per-key permissions. Per the auth docs, an OAuth app is used to call the API as a workspace user. The official MCP server is OAuth only.
result.access_detail: Pricing page shows a 7-day free trial with no credit card, then Foundation $45, Horizon $99 or custom Frontier per user per month. The page lists "API, Webhooks, Events, MCP, Custom channels" under the developer platform but does not say which plan includes them. I found no plan restriction on the API. Keys come from Settings → Machine users & agents.
result.api_notes: One GraphQL endpoint (POST https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1) with a public schema. Plain's UI is built on it, so the API has no limitations compared with the UI. The docs cover only the most used operations. A TypeScript SDK and webhooks exist.
result.blocker: Free access is a 7-day trial only. The pricing page does not say which paid plan includes API access. The vendor's own MCP server does not accept API keys (OAuth only).

evidence.quote: To call the API as a user in your workspace, use an OAuth app.
Each API key carries its own fine-grained permissions.
Start with a 7-day free trial, no credit card required.
Foundation is $45/user/month, Horizon is $99/user/month, and Frontier is custom.
This means that there are no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI.
Plain itself is built on this same GraphQL API.
Once connected, your AI client can do almost anything you can do in Plain, across nearly 400 tools.
You authenticate with your existing Plain account, so the MCP server has the same permissions as your user.
